title: Portable skill library: selection, prompt delivery and evidence
summary: A CLI-independent, versioned skills library built on pre-prompt-enrichment, with complete instruction delivery, per-invocation pins and receipts, reverse usage/outcome evidence, controlled quality comparisons and portable release bundles. Reconciles AGT-3465 and the prior skills architecture; thirteen sequential implementation slices.

openDecisions.title: Delivery authority
openDecisions.question: Who guarantees that fitting knowledge reaches the run?

options.A: Native CLI discovery owns selection and delivery.
options.B: Studio resolves and injects the complete bounded skill closure; native discovery is supplementary.
options.C: Inject the entire library into every prompt.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Studio resolves and injects the complete bounded skill closure; native discovery is supplementary.
openDecisions.rationale: The owner requires CLI-independent delivery and auditable context; complete selected closures meet it without whole-library noise.

openDecisions.title: Concept continuity
openDecisions.question: How should AGT-3465 and the earlier portable concept continue?

options.B: Use this Dossier as the umbrella, reconcile AGT-3465 criteria and merge its overlapping slices; retain source and decision history.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Use this Dossier as the umbrella, reconcile AGT-3465 criteria and merge its overlapping slices; retain source and decision history.
openDecisions.rationale: Rule delivery, card visibility and review need one receipt and one implementation backlog. Reconcile the unavailable original card before retiring work.

openDecisions.title: Instruction boundaries
openDecisions.question: What does whole skill mean?

options.A: Only SKILL.md; references may hide additional requirements.
options.B: SKILL.md plus every declared instructional reference, fully rendered; resources shipped as files.
options.C: Every package byte, including scripts and binary assets, enters the prompt.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. SKILL.md plus every declared instructional reference, fully rendered; resources shipped as files.
openDecisions.rationale: Required knowledge is complete and reviewable, while executable resources remain resources. Separate optional manuals into independently selectable modules.

openDecisions.title: Library ownership
openDecisions.question: How are scope and overrides resolved?

options.B: Product, workspace and project scopes with explicit qualified replacements/extensions and digest pins.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Product, workspace and project scopes with explicit qualified replacements/extensions and digest pins.
openDecisions.rationale: Supports customer knowledge and sharing while preserving provenance. Workspace activation is not a native CLI name-collision rule.

openDecisions.title: Selection policy
openDecisions.question: How should routing improve?

options.B: Typed triggers, fixed task-kind sets and forecast paths; one bounded model call only for ambiguity.
options.C: An unrestricted model reads the library for every run.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Typed triggers, fixed task-kind sets and forecast paths; one bounded model call only for ambiguity.
openDecisions.rationale: Deterministic routing stays cheap and explainable. The forecast is reused as a versioned fact, and a failed classifier has a conservative fallback.

openDecisions.title: Context budget
openDecisions.question: How should full delivery remain bounded?

options.A: Keep two optional blocks and 1,500 estimated tokens.
options.B: Target 800-1,800 tokens per skill; 6,000 default and 8,000 hard per-run addition, constrained by model context; migration procedure class up to 5,000.
options.C: No budget; rely on prompt caching.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Target 800-1,800 tokens per skill; 6,000 default and 8,000 hard per-run addition, constrained by model context; migration procedure class up to 5,000.
openDecisions.rationale: Supports complete useful instructions without truncation. Required overflow stops preparation. Cache savings do not reduce occupied context.

openDecisions.title: Evidence scope
openDecisions.question: What counts as skill use?

options.A: A skill listed, selected or echoed counts as loaded.
options.B: A successful managed transport receipt counts as delivered; native observations, prepared-only context and legacy summaries remain separate.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. A successful managed transport receipt counts as delivered; native observations, prepared-only context and legacy summaries remain separate.
openDecisions.rationale: Avoids fabricated usage. Count invocations, cards and requests separately and link immutable outcomes without double charging tokens.

openDecisions.title: Quality standard
openDecisions.question: What is sufficient to release a new default?

options.A: Usage growth and checking compliance with its own rules.
options.B: Structural and routing checks plus independent, blinded comparisons protecting correctness and content depth; domain-owned rollout/rollback.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Structural and routing checks plus independent, blinded comparisons protecting correctness and content depth; domain-owned rollout/rollback.
openDecisions.rationale: A skill can worsen results. Owner feedback and criterion-linked reviews produce testable revision candidates, not automatic edits to the live version.

openDecisions.title: Distribution and trust
openDecisions.question: How should installations exchange skills?

options.A: A marketplace owns installation and updates.
options.B: Versioned self-contained exports and release bundles with explicit adoption; optional plugins group skills and tool declarations.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Versioned self-contained exports and release bundles with explicit adoption; optional plugins group skills and tool declarations.
openDecisions.rationale: Works offline and across projects while preserving customer control. Imported scripts do not execute and connector grants remain separate.

openDecisions.title: Initial content and UI standard
openDecisions.question: Which guidance should be written first?

options.A: Promote the present visual-design skill universally.
options.B: Frontend best practice, backend best practice, then UX and visual standard; preserve existing hard rules and adopt the approved Access/one-look revision through a new version.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Frontend best practice, backend best practice, then UX and visual standard; preserve existing hard rules and adopt the approved Access/one-look revision through a new version.
openDecisions.rationale: Separates engineering and user-task quality, protects content depth, and gives the parallel visual standard a single distribution path.

Source: docs/portable-skill-library/index.html (AGT-4032). Read the Dossier, its evidence register, AGENTS.md and the indexed domain contracts for the touched area. Use each recommendation as the working choice unless a recorded operator decision selects another option; record the implemented options. Load fitting available skills. This is one promoted implementation slice, not authority to implement the whole programme. Keep task/workspace mutations behind the application API and Git ownership with the platform. Orchestration transition rules remain in orchestration-decisions/ and hosts apply typed decisions through the existing boundary. Do not add em dashes. Update affected contracts and docs index rows where required; avoid unrelated restyling.

## Scope

Author the content-first UX standard and pilot adoption seam.

Primary area: .agents/skills/ux-visual-standard/, project UI-policy dependency and visual comparison fixtures.

## Deliver

Create the third candidate using the Initial skills section. Put user task and information completeness first; include hierarchy, density, action semantics, disclosure, accessibility, status and feedback, current hard rules and flat admin grammar. Target about 1,800 closure tokens. The parallel Access/one-look work owns new standard decisions: if its approved revision is available, bind it by revision and test it; otherwise release a current-baseline candidate with an explicit unadopted pilot reference, not a fabricated dependency or an indefinite wait. Preserve useful capture/critique guidance as a narrow procedure. Turn the owner's content-depth blind comparison into a reproducible protected fixture using available original artefacts or a clearly labelled new representative case. Do not universalize landing-page aesthetics.

## Acceptance

- A content-heavy concept is not forced into implementation or decorative-layout instructions and retains every required acceptance item.
- UI behavior, relevant states, keyboard use, content coverage and both themes are included in evaluation evidence.
- Approved versus candidate visual standards are visibly distinct in package provenance and selection.
- No unseen owner comparison data is presented as a replicated measurement.

## Verification and result

Use relevant deterministic contract/unit tests and meaningful integration cases. For behavioral or visual frontend work run relevant Playwright coverage and retain screenshots in the task results folder. Runtime prompt changes need the matching live probe or a precise limitation. Keep TransitionDecisionBoundaryTests and MonolithDecisionBoundaryTests green if the decision boundary is touched. Report changed files, verification, documentation updates, selected Dossier options and remaining limits. Record this bounded slice in the Dossier implementation log.

implementationTasks.title: SL-11: Skill quality loop

criteria: A deliberately harmful candidate that improves visual compliance but drops required content fails promotion.
No mandatory policy is withheld; arm leakage, missing outputs and evaluator disagreements remain visible.
Every reported outcome has a cohort, denominator, version, evaluator and uncertainty; usage alone cannot trigger release.
Feedback creates a reviewed draft/revision path and cannot edit a published package in place.

## Scope

Export, import and customer-controlled package adoption.

Primary area: Product release packaging, workspace package API, import/export manifests and optional plugin container contract.

## Deliver

Implement deterministic archive export/import for exact packages and required dependencies, with licences, source provenance and review/evaluation receipts. Product releases ship baseline locks; private installation transfer uses the same format without a marketplace. A plugin manifest may group skills, assets and tool/connector requirements while keeping credentials and grants separate. Enforce hashes/signature or explicit local trust, schema and compatibility checks, containment, size bounds and a dry-run adoption preview. Customer forks retain upstream identity; upstream updates offer a three-way comparison and explicit lock adoption. Export private project knowledge only within explicit scope. Retain historical referenced packages and support rollback.

## Acceptance

- Round-trip export/import into an isolated installation preserves instruction and resource hashes offline.
- Malformed, unsigned-unadopted, incompatible, oversized and path-traversing packages do not activate or execute.
- Customer overrides survive product upgrade and produce distinct receipt lineage.
- No credentials, private card content, usage history or enabled connector grants leak through default export.

Publish an operator rollback procedure and domain documentation, update the earlier skills architecture and guide authoring contract, and retire only duplicate summary paths whose replacements are proven.
